turn.user_message: How is the summary drafted all through the stay?
turn.context: Automations place, turn 2 (playbook §5: tell me more, one level further down).

text: The night showed the summary appear on the evening round. It can, because it has been writing itself since admission.
Each day, Tojo records what happens to the patient. By the evening round, most of the summary is already there.
chat.note: The summary is written a little each day, not all at once.
prompts: Explain the first three steps on the round
Won’t this take our nurses’ time?
What if a report comes in late?
chat.pointer: Pick a day, or play the stay. The summary fills in, day by day.

blocks.title: The summary that writes itself
blocks.deck: One patient’s four days. Each day adds to the summary, so it is mostly written by the evening round.

kinds.name: On arrival
kinds.example: History, symptoms and what doctors found

kinds.name: Medicines
kinds.example: Given, changed and left over, in strips

kinds.name: Supplies
kinds.example: Used and left over, in whole units

kinds.name: Daily progress
kinds.example: The doctor’s notes on each round

kinds.name: Reasons and outcomes
kinds.example: Why each step was taken, and what happened

blocks.condition: The patient here is an example only. Your records would fill the summary the same way.

sheets.title: Admitted
sheets.text: Chest pain, admitted through Emergency. Blood tests and a heart tracing. Three medicines started.
sheets.entry: What is recorded on arrival at your hospital?

sheets.title: Tests
sheets.text: A heart scan shows a narrowed vessel. One medicine changed. A drip set and syringes used.
sheets.entry: Where do test results land today?

sheets.title: Procedure
sheets.text: A stent is placed in the narrowed vessel. A blood thinner is started. Stable after the procedure.

sheets.title: Evening round
sheets.text: The doctor says the patient can go tomorrow. Two strips of one medicine are left over.
sheets.entry: What does the doctor note on this round?
